judge_context: source_screen calls the 1900 census (MM8C-43Q, the record of the named assertions a_001 to a_006) misattributed: its leave-one-out score was 0.10. same_person on the same pair scores 0.91. The agent's rule: score it and decide it as usual, but a link to a record the screen calls misattributed is `speculative` at most.

Expected work: a scored link to I1 per named assertion at `speculative`, and each attachment link's `superseded_by` set to its new `pe_`. The `supersedes-named-attachment-links` and `screen-misattributed-cap` validators own the writes and the tier; do not re-check them. Linking at `probable` or `confident` ignores the screen's verdict and is a FAIL on Confidence calibration.

The rationale on each new link should name the screen's verdict alongside the same_person score and what matches; a rationale that cites the 0.91 score but not the misattributed verdict is a partial on rationale quality.
The 1910 record's John Becker assertions (a_035 to a_041) are not named; leaving their attachment links alone is correct.
